title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Billing Month's Late Fee on Demand Service Arrears
content:
## When this line stands to be raised

Where demand service invoicing on a rate program held under the Demand Service Rate Programs has gone
overdue, this month's late fee for that arrears stands to be put on the owner's account as one charge
line against the rate program. It is raised once for the billing month. The late fee line is raised
without a due day, and it is dated for payment when the billing month's invoice is issued.

## What the owner sees

A single demand service charge entry of the late fee kind is opened on the rate program, carrying the
money amount of the fee and the billing month it belongs to, so the owner owes that fee on the demand
service account and sees it as its own line rather than buried in another charge.

## Raising the line

The desk handles this itself: the tool `charge_overdue_late_fee_58988cf8` is unlocked and then called by
the agent, with the money amount of the fee worked out from the published terms and the records and
passed in. The tool raises the line; it does not work the fee out and does not judge whether the terms
allow it.

## The parameters

- `program_id` — the reference number of the demand service rate program the fee is charged against,
  read from the rate program lookup on the account.
- `late_fee_amount_usd` — the money amount of the late fee charged, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded
  half up at the cent and never negative.

## The receipt

One line of plain text comes back naming the reference number of the new demand service charge entry,
the billing month the fee belongs to and the fee amount in USD to 2 decimal places now standing on the
owner's demand service account. The named charge entry reference is the receipt that the fee line was
booked.
